whatThisIs: A statement of which artefacts in this evidence bundle relate to which control, so an auditor does not have to reverse-engineer it. It is a starting point for a conversation with an assessor, not a compliance verdict.
whatThisIsNot: This is NOT a certification. CAIRN holds no SOC 2 report and no ISO 27001 certificate, and none is in progress.

This is NOT an assertion that the organisation using CAIRN meets any control. The artefacts evidence what this software did; the control belongs to the organisation and its assessor decides whether the evidence satisfies it.

This is NOT a complete control set. Controls that a locally installed developer tool cannot speak to are listed as not-evidenced rather than omitted, because a map showing only the flattering controls is worse than no map.
Control titles are paraphrased for orientation. The authoritative text is the framework's, not this file's.
operatorOverride: Copy this file to vault/controlMap.json to amend it. The bundle records which copy it used, and the amended file is hashed and signed with the rest of the bundle.

controls.title: Record-keeping — automatic recording of events over the system's lifetime
evidencedBy: ledger.jsonl — every authorisation decision, allow and deny alike, hash-chained to its predecessor
spans.jsonl — what executed after each decision, correlated by traceId
audit.jsonl — the surrounding event narrative for the same window
integrity.json — whether the chain verified at export time
doesNotEvidence: Completeness. Hashing a ledger detects alteration of what is present; it cannot detect a record that was never written. Completeness rests on the governance gate being the sole execution path.
When a record was written. Timestamps are asserted by the host clock and are not externally attested, so sequence is evidence and wall-clock time is not.

controls.title: Human oversight — the system is designed so a person can oversee, intervene and interrupt
evidencedBy: ledger.jsonl — decisions refused by policy, recorded with the rule that refused them and not overridable by user approval
ledger.jsonl — payload.policyContext.corporatePolicy.mandatoryApproval, naming the human who approved or refused an action a signed policy required approval for
audit.jsonl — CORPORATE_APPROVAL_GRANTED and CORPORATE_APPROVAL_REFUSED events
doesNotEvidence: Graduated autonomy. There is no autonomy ladder; an action is permitted or refused, and there is no per-action maximum autonomy level derived from policy.

That the oversight was well-informed. CAIRN grades risk from the mechanism of an action — the tool's capability class and a static scan of the code — and not from what the action would affect. A person approving a MEDIUM-risk script is not being told its blast radius, because the system does not model one.

controls.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
evidencedBy: ledger.jsonl — payload.findings, the static-scan findings that raised an action's risk grade
ledger.jsonl — refusals where code could not be read and was therefore graded unsafe rather than assumed safe
spans.jsonl — execution outcome and duration, including failures
doesNotEvidence: Accuracy of model output. Nothing in this bundle establishes that an answer was correct. CAIRN's assurance grades describe how thoroughly an action was VERIFIED — static-only, sandbox-executed, deterministic — which is a statement about execution, not about truth.
Robustness under adversarial input. No adversarial evaluation has been run against this installation.

controls.title: Logical access security — identification, authentication and protection of information assets
evidencedBy: ledger.jsonl — actor, resolved from the operating system principal (Windows SID where available) and not from anything the model can influence
ledger.jsonl — payload.capability, the capability class the action required and the principal held
doesNotEvidence: Authentication strength. CAIRN is a single-user desktop application; it inherits the operating system session and performs no authentication of its own. There is no SSO, no MFA and no session management.

controls.title: Registration and authorisation of new users before access is issued
doesNotEvidence: There is no user provisioning in CAIRN. No accounts are created, granted or revoked, so no artefact in this bundle speaks to this control.

controls.title: Least privilege — access to data and functions based on role, and its modification and removal
evidencedBy: ledger.jsonl — capability classes (read / write / execute), with an unclassified tool treated as the most restrictive
ledger.jsonl — corporate policy refusals for forbiddenPaths and allowedPathPrefixes, where an organisation confined work to declared roots
ledger.jsonl — package capability refusals, where an installed package attempted something it had not declared
doesNotEvidence: Role-based access control. Roles exist as a local label only; `rbac.local` is an entitlement string with no implementation behind it.
Segregation of duties. There is one principal, so there is nothing to segregate.

controls.title: Physical access to facilities and protected information assets
doesNotEvidence: A physical control. Software running on an operator's own machine cannot evidence it, and the organisation's own facility controls apply instead.

controls.title: Disposal of physical assets containing protected information
doesNotEvidence: A physical control, as above. Note that the ledger, audit stream and vault live on the host, so the host's disposal procedure governs them.

controls.title: Logical access measures against threats from outside the system boundary
evidencedBy: ledger.jsonl — every tool invocation passed a default-deny gate before running; a tool cannot execute without traversing it
audit.jsonl — egress decisions, including refusals where a payload matched a secret pattern
ledger.jsonl — corporate policy lockdown refusals where a signed policy could not be verified
doesNotEvidence: Network boundary controls. CAIRN does not manage firewalls, network segmentation or inbound access, and no artefact here describes them.

controls.title: Restriction of the transmission, movement and removal of information
evidencedBy: audit.jsonl — cloud egress decisions with the classification that produced them, and the refusals
ledger.jsonl — CLOUD_SPEND records showing which provider and model were reached, and at what cost
doesNotEvidence: That transmission was encrypted. Providers are reached over HTTPS, but this bundle collects no evidence of the transport used.

That nothing left the machine. Local-first is a posture, not a default: unless the operator has configured otherwise, the routing prompt — which carries the user's message and the vault index — is sent to a cloud router on each turn. The privacy posture in the product states the live setting.

controls.title: Prevention or detection of unauthorised or malicious software
evidencedBy: ledger.jsonl — payload.findings from the static scan of what an invocation would actually run, including the resolved contents of a script invoked by name
ledger.jsonl — refusals where an EXECUTE action referenced code the gate could not read, which is graded unsafe rather than assumed safe
audit.jsonl — script integrity events, where a vault script changed against its recorded hash
ledger.jsonl — corporate blocklist refusals, where a signed policy forbade a command found in the resolved payload
doesNotEvidence: Anti-malware coverage of the host. CAIRN inspects what it is asked to run; it does not scan the machine.
That the static scan is complete. It is advisory and pattern-based: a clean scan means these specific checks did not fire, not that the code is safe. That sentence is in the scan output itself.
